name: AZ-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Greg Stanton holds a lopsided financial edge: $1.9 million on hand versus about $116,000 for Zuhdi Jasser
District fundamentals favor Democrats: a D+4 lean plus a favorable national environment
Prediction markets price Stanton's win probability near 96%
No public polling or outside spending against Stanton signals a contest
model.rationale: Stanton combines incumbency, a D+4 district, and a cash advantage of more than sixteen to one, with no outside groups opposing him; markets price the race near 96% Democratic. With no polling to the contrary, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Stanton or fresh polling showing a single-digit race would be the main signal to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arizona's 4th District leans Democratic, and incumbent Greg Stanton is seeking re-election with a substantial financial edge. He has raised about $2.6 million and holds $1.9 million on hand, while Republican Zuhdi Jasser has raised roughly $730,000 with about $116,000 available. No outside groups are spending against Stanton, and no independent polling of the general election is available.

Prediction markets give Stanton roughly a 96% chance of winning, and the district's fundamentals point the same way: a D+4 partisan lean, a favorable national environment for Democrats, and the usual incumbency advantage. Jasser, a physician and commentator known from prior statewide runs, has not attracted outside support. A third-party candidate is also on the ballot but is not a factor. Absent a major external shock, this race sits safely in the Democratic column.
